newsitem.title: DENMARK: Border blockade hits Danish Xmas tree exports.
newsitem.headline: Border blockade hits Danish Xmas tree exports.

text.p: Danish Christmas tree growers on Tuesday said lorry-drivers blockading the border with Germany had left almost a million export-bound trees rotting at the frontier, dealing a serious blow to the industry.
The protest, against government plans to cut drivers' overseas subsistence allowances, was unrelated to French drivers' nationwide roadblock protests.

"The blockade is nothing short of a catastrophe for our business just ahead of the festive season. We normally send 300 trucks full of Christmas trees and spruce to the south every day at this time of the year," a spokesman for Denmark's Christmas Tree Growers' Association told Reuters on Tuesday.

"Apart from the risk of fire, Christmas trees and spruce tightly packed into trucks rot away after a few days. We reckon that some 600 trucks carrying Christmas greenery have been stuck at the Danish-German border since the weekend," he said.

Each lorry carried an average of 1,500 trees, giving a total of around 900,000, he added. They were among an estimated 1,500 Danish vehicles whose drivers blockaded the Padborg border customs area for the second day on Tuesday.
Denmark is Europe's biggest exporter of Christmas trees, selling six million trees and 25,000 tonnes of spruce branches abroad and earning 500 million Danish crowns ($86 million) a year.
Germany, the main market, takes over 60 percent of Danish export production.
